discovery: Quantum simulation and quantum information processing with controlled atoms: theoretical foundations and the realization of strongly correlated quantum matter in optical lattices

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed in 1995 that individually controlled atoms could serve as a quantum computer, proposing the trapped-ion gate that launched experimental quantum information science. Zoller, Cirac and coworkers then showed in 1998 that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model, which turned quantum many-body physics into a programmable laboratory discipline. Bloch made this vision real. He observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition (2002), developed single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy, and established optical lattices as analog quantum simulators of magnetism, localization and nonequilibrium dynamics. Together their work created a new field: synthetic quantum matter in which Hamiltonians are engineered, controlled and read out atom by atom. Today's ion-trap, neutral-atom and Rydberg-array processors, including demonstrations of error-corrected logical qubits, rest directly on these conceptual and experimental foundations. Their contributions connect fundamental many-body physics with quantum technology.
